analysis:
Reviewed SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift (base vs head) and the recency tests. The only behavioral change is in scanOnDisk and removeCorrupt. Corrupt-file removal is split into a private removeFile(tag) helper, which does the same performIndexedRemoval, removeItemIfSafe and index.remove as before, and removeCorrupt, which calls it and then increments corruptDropped. The TTL check at scan time moved out of the validation guard into its own guard. A file whose mtime is past the TTL is now removed via removeFile and not counted as corrupt. Before, it was removed through removeCorrupt and counted. The header, weightHash, layoutEpoch, blockSize and lookupTag-prefix checks still route to removeCorrupt and still count.

Security-relevant checks for T-041 (at-rest cache):
- TTL enforcement at restart is preserved: expired files are still unlinked through the same safe, ownership-guarded path (performIndexedRemoval, removeItemIfSafe under root) and are never inserted into the index.
- The fileCoordinator.tryAcquire access is still held, with defer release, across both paths.
- There is no change to the crypto, HMAC names, DBK3 format, TTL value, epoch handling or the capability advertisement. Per-file removal still does not rotate the epoch.
- The only difference is stat accounting. corruptDropped no longer includes TTL expiries, so any alerting that relied on it would see fewer events. That is diagnostic, not a security control, and it is not a material regression.
- The new test asserts that real corruption (3 garbage bytes) still increments corruptDropped and removes the file. That is the correct fail-closed behavior.

The test file changes add assertions only. No finding. Callers of corruptDropped outside the supplied evidence were not examined, but the metric appears non-security-bearing.
